questions.q: What did Jesus use to feed the five thousand?
options: Seven loaves and a jar of oil
Twelve loaves and a basket of figs
questions.why: The Gospels say he blessed five loaves and two fish, and twelve baskets of leftovers were gathered.

questions.q: Which rite, using water, marks a person's entry into the Church?
questions.why: Baptism is the rite of initiation in nearly all churches; Peter calls the crowd at Pentecost to repent and be baptised.

questions.q: Which disciple agreed to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver?
questions.why: Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests, who weighed out thirty pieces of silver.

questions.q: Which festival celebrates the resurrection of Jesus?
questions.why: Easter, the oldest and chief Christian feast, celebrates Jesus rising from the dead on the third day.

questions.q: What is the season of fasting and penitence before Easter called?
questions.why: Lent lasts about forty days, echoing Jesus' forty days in the wilderness; Advent is the season before Christmas.

questions.q: Which apostle wrote the letters to the Romans and the Corinthians?
questions.why: Paul is named as the author of Romans and of 1 and 2 Corinthians, which open with his greeting.

questions.q: Which prayer begins "Our Father in heaven"?
questions.why: Jesus taught it to his disciples in the Sermon on the Mount; Luke gives a shorter form.

questions.q: What is the Christian doctrine that God is one God in three persons called?
questions.why: The Trinity holds that Father, Son and Holy Spirit are one God; the Incarnation is the doctrine that the Son became human.

questions.q: What does the word "gospel" mean?
questions.why: "Gospel" comes from Old English godspel, translating the Greek euangelion, "good news".

questions.q: On which body of water did Jesus walk, according to the Gospels?
questions.why: The disciples were rowing across the Sea of Galilee (Tiberias) when they saw Jesus walking on the water.

questions.q: What is the meal Jesus shared with his disciples on the night before he died usually called?
questions.why: At the Last Supper Jesus broke bread and shared the cup, words churches repeat at Communion.

questions.q: For how many days did Jesus fast in the wilderness before he was tempted?
questions.why: Matthew says he fasted forty days and forty nights, echoing Moses and Elijah.

questions.q: In which parable does a traveller from a despised people help a man beaten by robbers?
questions.why: Jesus told it to answer "Who is my neighbour?"; a priest and a Levite pass by, but a Samaritan stops to help.

questions.q: What is the title of the head of the Roman Catholic Church?
questions.why: The Pope is the Bishop of Rome; Catholics regard him as the successor of Peter.

questions.q: On what date do most Western churches celebrate Christmas?
questions.why: Western churches keep Christmas on 25 December; many Orthodox churches on the older Julian calendar keep it on what is now 7 January.

questions.q: Which creed begins "I believe in God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth" and is used at baptisms in the Western church?
questions.why: The Apostles' Creed grew from the old Roman baptismal creed; the Nicene Creed begins "We believe in one God".

questions.q: In which year did Martin Luther publish his Ninety-five Theses, traditionally counted as the start of the Reformation?
questions.why: Luther's theses against the sale of indulgences are dated 31 October 1517.

questions.q: How many sacraments does the Catholic Church recognise?
questions.why: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Penance, Anointing of the Sick, Holy Orders and Matrimony; most Protestants keep two.

questions.q: In which year is the Great Schism between the Eastern and Western churches traditionally dated?
questions.why: In 1054 papal legates and the Patriarch of Constantinople excommunicated each other; the split hardened over the following centuries.

questions.q: Who was the first Christian martyr, according to Acts?
questions.why: Stephen, one of the seven chosen to serve, was stoned after his speech to the council.

questions.q: What is the Catholic doctrine that the bread and wine of the Eucharist become the body and blood of Christ called?
questions.why: The Fourth Lateran Council (1215) used the term, and Trent reaffirmed it; consubstantiation is a label often applied to the Lutheran view.

questions.q: What happened to the apostles at Pentecost, according to Acts?
options: Jesus ascended into heaven before them
The Holy Spirit came upon them
They were freed from prison by an angel
questions.why: Tongues like fire rested on them and they spoke in other languages; the Ascension happened earlier, in Acts 1.

questions.q: Which bishop of Hippo wrote the Confessions and The City of God?
questions.why: Augustine (354-430), bishop of Hippo in North Africa, is the most influential Latin church father.

questions.q: Which apostle said he would not believe in the resurrection unless he touched the wounds?
questions.why: Thomas doubted until Jesus appeared eight days later and invited him to touch the wounds.

questions.q: On which island was John when he received the visions of Revelation?
questions.why: John says he was on the isle called Patmos "because of God's Word and the testimony of Jesus".

questions.q: Which English king broke with Rome and was declared Supreme Head of the Church of England in 1534?
questions.why: The Act of Supremacy of 1534 made Henry VIII head of the English church after the Pope refused to annul his marriage.

questions.q: Which Reformation slogan means that a sinner is justified by faith alone?
questions.why: Sola fide (faith alone) stood beside sola scriptura (Scripture alone) as a central Protestant principle.

questions.q: Which Roman emperor, with Licinius, issued the Edict of Milan granting toleration to Christians in 313?
questions.why: Constantine and Licinius agreed the Edict of Milan; Theodosius later made Nicene Christianity the state religion in 380.

questions.q: Which Jewish festival was being kept when Jesus held the Last Supper, according to the Synoptic Gospels?
questions.why: Matthew, Mark and Luke present the Last Supper as a Passover meal.

questions.q: Which thirteenth-century Dominican wrote the Summa Theologiae?
questions.why: Thomas Aquinas (c. 1225-1274) left the Summa Theologiae unfinished at his death; it became the classic of Catholic theology.

questions.q: Which Gospel do most New Testament scholars regard as the earliest written?
questions.why: Most scholars hold Markan priority: Matthew and Luke used Mark as a source. Church tradition long placed Matthew first.

questions.q: Which council in 451 defined Christ as one person "in two natures", divine and human?
questions.why: The Chalcedonian Definition of 451 was rejected by the Oriental Orthodox churches, who are often called non-Chalcedonian.

questions.q: The phrase "the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one", printed in the King James Version but missing from the early Greek manuscripts, is in which book?
questions.why: The "Johannine Comma" in 1 John 5:7-8 is found in late Latin manuscripts but not in the early Greek ones, so modern translations such as the WEB leave it out.

questions.q: At which verse do Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus end the Gospel of Mark?
questions.why: These two fourth-century codices end with the women fleeing the tomb in fear; verses 9-20 are missing from them.

questions.q: In which Gospel is the story of the woman caught in adultery now printed, although it is absent from the earliest manuscripts?
questions.why: The passage (John 7:53-8:11) is missing from the earliest Greek manuscripts, and some later ones place it elsewhere.

questions.q: Whose Easter letter of 367 is the earliest surviving list of exactly the 27 books of the New Testament?
questions.why: Athanasius' 39th Festal Letter lists the same 27 books found in New Testaments today.

questions.q: Which second-century teacher rejected the Old Testament and used a canon of an edited Luke and ten letters of Paul?
questions.why: Marcion of Sinope set the God of the Old Testament against the Father of Jesus; his canon pushed the church to define its own.

questions.q: Which word, added to the Nicene Creed in the West, says the Spirit proceeds "and from the Son"?
questions.why: The filioque spread from Spain (Toledo, 589) and was a lasting point of dispute with the Eastern churches.

questions.q: The Council of Nicaea was called mainly to deal with the teaching of which Alexandrian presbyter?
questions.why: Arius taught that the Son was created; Nicaea answered that he is "of one substance" (homoousios) with the Father.

questions.q: Before which emperor did Luther refuse to recant at the Diet of Worms in 1521?
questions.why: Charles V presided at Worms; afterwards the Edict of Worms declared Luther an outlaw. Frederick the Wise was the elector who protected him.

questions.q: Matthew names Jacob as Joseph's father. Whom does Luke's genealogy name?
questions.why: Luke calls Jesus "the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli", while Matthew 1:16 has Jacob; interpreters have long offered ways to reconcile the two.

questions.q: Which British monk did Augustine oppose for teaching that people can avoid sin without the help of grace?
questions.why: Pelagius' teaching was condemned at the Council of Carthage (418) and later at Ephesus (431).

questions.q: Which council in 431 affirmed that Mary may be called Theotokos, "God-bearer", against Nestorius?
questions.why: Nestorius preferred "Christ-bearer"; the Council of Ephesus deposed him and upheld Theotokos.

questions.q: Near which Egyptian town was the Coptic library containing the Gospel of Thomas found in 1945?
questions.why: The Nag Hammadi codices were found in 1945; Greek fragments of Thomas had been found earlier at Oxyrhynchus, and Qumran is the site of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

questions.q: Matthew 27:9 says a prophecy about thirty pieces of silver was spoken by Jeremiah. Which prophet's book contains the closest wording?
questions.why: The thirty pieces of silver thrown to the potter come from Zechariah 11:12-13; interpreters link Matthew's citation of Jeremiah to Jeremiah's potter and field passages.

questions.q: How many surahs does the Quran have?
questions.why: The Quran has 114 surahs (chapters) of very different lengths.

questions.q: In which city is the Kaaba?
questions.why: The Kaaba stands in the Sacred Mosque in Mecca; Medina is the city of the Prophet's mosque.

questions.q: In which month do Muslims fast from dawn to sunset?
questions.why: The Quran commands fasting in Ramadan, the month in which it was revealed.

questions.q: What is a Muslim place of communal prayer called?
questions.why: Masjid means "place of prostration"; the minaret is its tower and the mihrab the niche showing the direction of prayer.

questions.q: What is the pilgrimage to Mecca, required once in a lifetime of those able, called?
questions.why: Hajj is a duty for those who can make the journey; Umrah is a lesser pilgrimage that can be made at any time.

questions.q: According to the Quran, which prophet raised the foundations of the Kaaba with his son Ishmael?
questions.why: The Quran describes Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the House and praying for it to be accepted.

questions.q: To which city did Muhammad and his followers migrate in the Hijra?
questions.why: The city then called Yathrib became Madinat al-Nabi, "the city of the Prophet".

questions.q: What is the obligatory giving of alms, one of the Five Pillars, called?
questions.why: Zakat is a fixed share of wealth given each year; sadaqa is voluntary charity.

questions.q: Which prophet does the Quran call "the Messiah"?
questions.why: The angels give Mary glad tidings of a word from God whose name is "the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary".

questions.q: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan?
questions.why: Eid al-Fitr, the feast of breaking the fast, falls on the first day of Shawwal; Eid al-Adha comes at the Hajj.

questions.q: What is the declaration "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God" called?
questions.why: The Shahada is the first of the five things on which, in the hadith, Islam is built.

questions.q: Which meat does the Quran forbid Muslims to eat?
questions.why: It forbids carrion, blood, swine flesh and what is offered to other than God, with an exception for necessity.

questions.q: What is the direction Muslims face in prayer called?
questions.why: The qibla is the direction of the Kaaba; the Quran records the change from Jerusalem to the Sacred Mosque.

questions.q: Which woman has a surah of the Quran named after her?
questions.why: Surah 19, Maryam, tells of the birth of Jesus.

questions.q: What is the call to prayer, given from the mosque, called?
questions.why: The adhan is the public call; the iqama is the second call given just before prayer begins, and the khutba is the sermon.

questions.q: Who became the first caliph after Muhammad's death, according to Sunni Muslims?
questions.why: Abu Bakr was chosen at the Saqifa in 632; Shia Muslims hold that Ali should have succeeded.

questions.q: Which treaty of 628 set a truce between the Muslims and the Quraysh of Mecca?
questions.why: At Hudaybiyyah the Muslims agreed to put off their pilgrimage for a year; tradition links Surah al-Fath (48) to it.

questions.q: Which battle of 624 was the first major victory of the Muslims over the Quraysh?
questions.why: At Badr a small Muslim force defeated a larger Meccan army; Uhud (625) went against the Muslims.

questions.q: In which cave, near Mecca, did Muhammad receive the first revelation?
questions.why: Tradition says the first words revealed in the cave of Hira were "Read: In the name of thy Lord"; Thawr is where he hid during the Hijra.

questions.q: Which surah opens with the Night Journey from the Sacred Mosque to the "Farthest Mosque"?
questions.why: Surah 17 is named al-Isra, "the Night Journey", after its first verse.

questions.q: Who compiled the hadith collection that Sunni Muslims regard as the most authentic after the Quran?
questions.why: Sahih al-Bukhari is ranked first among the Sunni collections, with Sahih Muslim close behind.

questions.q: Whom do Shia Muslims regard as the first Imam?
questions.why: For the Shia, Ali, cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, was his rightful successor; Husayn was the third Imam.

questions.q: During Hajj, pilgrims walk seven times between which two hills?
questions.why: This walk, the sa'i, recalls Hagar's search for water for Ishmael.

questions.q: In which part of Ramadan is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) traditionally sought?
options: Among the odd nights of the last ten
On the first night of the month
On the night of the full moon, the 15th
questions.why: Surah 97 says the Quran was sent down on this night; hadith tell Muslims to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan.

questions.q: Who was Muhammad's first wife?
questions.why: Khadijah, a merchant of Mecca, married him about fifteen years before the first revelation and was the first to believe.

questions.q: Which verse is known as the Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi)?
questions.why: It begins "Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal" and speaks of his Throne extending over the heavens and the earth. 24:35 is the Light Verse.

questions.q: Eid al-Adha recalls which prophet's readiness to sacrifice his son?
questions.why: The Quran says God ransomed the son "with a tremendous victim"; Muslims sacrifice an animal at the feast.

questions.q: What is the ritual washing of face, hands, head and feet before prayer called?
questions.why: Wudu is the minor ablution; ghusl is the full bath, and tayammum uses clean earth when there is no water.

questions.q: On which day do Muslims hold their weekly congregational prayer?
questions.why: The Quran calls believers to hasten to the prayer "of the day of congregation" (al-Jumu'ah) and leave trading.

questions.q: Which prophet was swallowed by a fish, according to the Quran?
questions.why: Surah 37 tells how the fish swallowed Yunus; Surah 10 is named after him.

questions.q: In which year CE was Husayn ibn Ali killed at Karbala?
questions.why: Husayn died on 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE); Shia Muslims mourn him each year on Ashura.

questions.q: After Hafs 'an 'Asim, which transmitted reading of the Quran is most widely printed, especially in North and West Africa?
questions.why: Warsh's transmission from Nafi' of Medina is standard in much of the Maghreb and West Africa; Hafs dominates elsewhere.

questions.q: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, whom did Abu Bakr ask to collect the Quran after the Battle of Yamama?
questions.why: Umar feared that the deaths of reciters at Yamama would lose parts of the Quran, and Zayd, who had written revelation for the Prophet, was given the task.

questions.q: According to Sunni tradition, which caliph had standard copies of the Quran sent to the provinces and other copies burned?
questions.why: Prompted by Hudhayfa's alarm at differences in recitation, Uthman had copies made from Hafsa's sheets and ordered other manuscripts burned.

questions.q: Where was the palimpsest whose lower text differs in places from the standard Uthmanic Quran found in 1972?
questions.why: The Sanaa palimpsest was found in a store of old manuscripts in the Great Mosque of Sanaa, Yemen.

questions.q: Who wrote The Incoherence of the Philosophers?
questions.why: Al-Ghazali (d. 1111) attacked the philosophers; Ibn Rushd replied with The Incoherence of the Incoherence.

questions.q: Which of these schools of law is followed by Twelver Shia Muslims?
questions.why: The Ja'fari school is named after the sixth Imam, Ja'far al-Sadiq; the other three are Sunni schools, with the Hanbali.

questions.q: Which Abbasid caliph began the Mihna, the inquisition requiring scholars to affirm that the Quran was created?
questions.why: Al-Ma'mun began it in 833; Ahmad ibn Hanbal refused to comply, and al-Mutawakkil ended it.

questions.q: Which verse is most often cited as the basis for abrogation (naskh) in the Quran?
questions.why: It says that whatever verse God abrogates or causes to be forgotten, he brings one better or like it.

questions.q: The reports known as the "Satanic verses" incident are connected with verses about al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat. In which surah are those verses?
questions.why: Some early historians, including al-Tabari, record the story; many Muslim scholars reject it. Surah 22:52 is sometimes linked to it but does not name the goddesses.

questions.q: By what title do Twelver Shia call the twelfth Imam, whom they believe to be in occultation?
questions.why: They hold that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, al-Mahdi, went into occultation and will return; al-Sadiq, al-Rida and al-Baqir are titles of earlier Imams.

questions.q: Which group broke away from Ali after he agreed to arbitration following the Battle of Siffin?
questions.why: The Kharijites ("those who went out") rejected arbitration in 657; one of them later killed Ali in 661.

questions.q: According to reports in Sahih al-Bukhari, which surahs did Ibn Mas'ud hold were not part of the Quran?
questions.why: Ubayy ibn Ka'b answered that the Prophet had recited them as Quran. The surahs are in the Quran as Muslims have it.

questions.q: Al-Bukhari, compiler of the Sahih, took his name from which city?
questions.why: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (810-870) was born in Bukhara, in today's Uzbekistan; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj came from Nishapur.

questions.q: At which place do Shia Muslims hold that Muhammad declared, "Whoever I am his mawla, Ali is his mawla"?
questions.why: The words are reported on the way back from the Farewell Pilgrimage in 632. Shia read them as appointing Ali; Sunnis generally read mawla as friend or ally.

questions.q: What are the first five books of the Hebrew Bible together called?
questions.why: The Torah (Genesis to Deuteronomy) is read in the synagogue each year from a handwritten scroll.

questions.q: What is the Jewish name for the Hebrew Bible, formed from the initials of its three parts?
questions.why: Torah, Nevi'im (Prophets) and Ketuvim (Writings) give T-N-K, Tanakh.

questions.q: Which eight-day festival, with candles lit on a menorah, is known as the Festival of Lights?
questions.why: Hanukkah recalls the rededication of the Temple in the time of the Maccabees.

questions.q: What is the ritual meal held on the first night(s) of Passover called?
questions.why: At the Seder families retell the Exodus and eat matzah and bitter herbs, as Exodus commands.

questions.q: Which instrument, made from a ram's horn, is sounded on Rosh Hashanah?
questions.why: The Torah calls the day a memorial "of blowing of trumpets"; the rabbis require the ram's-horn shofar.

questions.q: At what age does a Jewish boy traditionally become bar mitzvah?
questions.why: At 13 a boy becomes responsible for the commandments; for girls the bat mitzvah age is 12.

questions.q: What is food that meets Jewish dietary law called?
questions.why: Kosher means "fit"; treif is forbidden food, and pareve is food that is neither meat nor dairy.

questions.q: In which book of the Torah does the Shema, "Hear, O Israel", appear?
questions.why: Deuteronomy 6:4 is the first line of the Shema, recited morning and evening.

questions.q: Which festival celebrates the story of Esther saving the Jews of Persia?
questions.why: The name comes from pur, the lot Haman cast to choose the day for his plot.

questions.q: To whom did God give the two stone tablets on Mount Sinai?
questions.why: Exodus says God gave Moses "the two tablets of the covenant", written with God's finger.

questions.q: Who was the father of Isaac?
questions.why: Abraham named his son by Sarah Isaac; Jacob was Isaac's son.

questions.q: The Western Wall in Jerusalem is part of the retaining walls of which ancient site?
options: The Temple Mount of the Second Temple
questions.why: It survives from Herod's enlargement of the Temple Mount; the Temple itself was destroyed in 70 CE.

questions.q: During which festival do Jews dwell in temporary booths?
questions.why: Leviticus commands dwelling in booths for seven days, recalling the wilderness journey.

questions.q: What is the braided bread traditionally eaten at Sabbath meals?
questions.why: Two challah loaves recall the double portion of manna given before the Sabbath; matzah is the unleavened bread of Passover.

questions.q: Which sea parted for the Israelites as they fled Egypt?
questions.why: The Hebrew yam suf is usually translated Red Sea; many render it "Sea of Reeds".

questions.q: Who is credited with compiling the Mishnah around 200 CE?
questions.why: Rabbi Judah the Prince edited the Mishnah; Rav Ashi is linked with the editing of the Babylonian Talmud.

questions.q: Which prophet told King David "You are the man!" after David's sin with Bathsheba?
questions.why: Nathan's parable of the poor man's lamb led David to condemn himself.

questions.q: Which king's army destroyed Solomon's Temple?
questions.why: In Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year his captain Nebuzaradan burned the Temple, in 587 or 586 BCE.

questions.q: In which year did the Romans destroy the Second Temple?
questions.why: Titus' army took Jerusalem in 70 CE; 586 BCE is the Babylonian destruction, and 135 CE the end of the Bar Kokhba revolt.

questions.q: Which fast day mourns the destruction of both Temples?
questions.why: Tisha B'Av, the ninth of Av, is the traditional date of both destructions.

questions.q: Rashi, the great commentator on the Torah and Talmud, lived in which country?
questions.why: Rashi (1040-1105) lived in Troyes in Champagne; his commentary is printed in almost every Talmud and many Bibles.

questions.q: What did Hillel tell the man who asked to be taught the whole Torah on one foot?
options: Love the Lord your God with all your heart
Do not separate yourself from the community
What is hateful to you, do not do to another
questions.why: Hillel added: "That is the entire Torah, and the rest is its interpretation. Go study." Shammai had pushed the man away.

questions.q: What is the small parchment scroll fixed to a Jewish doorpost called?
questions.why: It holds the Shema passages, following the command to write the words on the doorposts of the house.

questions.q: Which Persian king allowed the Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the Temple?
questions.why: Ezra opens with the proclamation of Cyrus in his first year, around 538 BCE.

questions.q: What is the rabbinic genre of biblical interpretation found in works like Genesis Rabbah called?
questions.why: Midrash interprets the Bible verse by verse, with both legal (halakhic) and narrative (aggadic) material.

questions.q: The rule against mixing meat and milk is derived from a verse forbidding what?
options: Eating the sinew of the thigh
Eating animals that do not chew the cud
Boiling a young goat in its mother's milk
questions.why: The verse appears three times in the Torah; the rabbis read it as forbidding cooking, eating and benefiting from meat with milk.

questions.q: Against which Seleucid ruler did the Maccabees revolt?
questions.why: Antiochus IV banned Jewish practice and defiled the Temple; the Maccabees rededicated it in 164 BCE.

questions.q: Which Jewish movement began in nineteenth-century Germany and treats traditional law as non-binding?
questions.why: Reform began in German congregations in the early 1800s; Karaism is a much older movement that rejects the rabbinic Oral Torah.

questions.q: How many adults are needed for a minyan, the quorum for public prayer?
questions.why: Orthodox practice counts ten men; most non-Orthodox movements count women too.

questions.q: How many days after Passover is the festival of Shavuot?
questions.why: The Torah commands counting seven weeks, fifty days; the rabbis link Shavuot with the giving of the Torah at Sinai.

questions.q: According to the opening of Pirkei Avot, Moses received the Torah at Sinai and handed it on to whom?
questions.why: The chain runs from Moses to Joshua, the elders, the prophets and the Men of the Great Assembly.

questions.q: Maimonides' Thirteen Principles of Faith appear in his commentary on which chapter of the Mishnah?
questions.why: The chapter opens "All Israel have a share in the World to Come", and Maimonides set out the beliefs he held were required for it.

questions.q: According to the Talmud, which sage asked Vespasian to spare Yavneh and its sages?
questions.why: Smuggled out of besieged Jerusalem, he asked for "Yavneh and its Sages", which became the centre of rabbinic learning after 70 CE.

questions.q: Which sage is said to have hailed Simon bar Kosiba (Bar Kokhba) as the messiah?
questions.why: The Jerusalem Talmud (Taanit 4) reports Akiva's words and another sage's rebuke; the revolt was crushed in 135 CE.

questions.q: After three years of dispute between the schools of Hillel and Shammai, what did the heavenly voice declare, according to Eruvin 13b?
options: Both are the words of the living God, but the law follows Hillel
Neither school may rule until Elijah comes
Each city should follow its own school
questions.why: The Talmud goes on to say Hillel's school was favoured because they were humble and taught Shammai's views first.

questions.q: Who wrote the glosses (the Mappah) that adapt Joseph Karo's Shulchan Arukh to Ashkenazi custom?
questions.why: Isserles of Kraków (the Rema) added Ashkenazi practice to Karo's Sephardi code in the sixteenth century.

questions.q: To which second-century sage is the Zohar traditionally attributed?
questions.why: Tradition credits Shimon bar Yochai; most academic scholars date it to thirteenth-century Spain, linked with Moses de León.

questions.q: What is the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible in the Masoretic tradition, dated 1008 or 1009 CE?
questions.why: The Aleppo Codex is older (tenth century) but has lost much of its Torah; Sinaiticus is a Greek Christian Bible.

questions.q: Which biblical book survives complete among the Dead Sea Scrolls?
questions.why: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) from Qumran Cave 1 holds all 66 chapters; other books survive only in parts.

questions.q: Which institution in New York is the main seminary of Conservative Judaism?
questions.why: JTS was reshaped under Solomon Schechter from 1902; Hebrew Union College trains Reform rabbis and Yeshiva University is Modern Orthodox.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the founder of Hasidism?
options: Israel ben Eliezer, the Baal Shem Tov
questions.why: The Baal Shem Tov taught in eighteenth-century Podolia; the Vilna Gaon led the opposition to Hasidism.

questions.q: Which seventeenth-century messianic claimant shocked his followers by converting to Islam in 1666?
questions.why: Brought before the Ottoman sultan, Shabbetai Zevi converted; Jacob Frank, a century later, led his followers into Catholicism.

questions.q: Which Hebrew word in Isaiah 7:14, rendered "virgin" in many Christian Bibles, means a young woman?
questions.why: The Hebrew has 'almah, a young woman; the Septuagint translated it parthenos. Betulah is the more specific Hebrew word for a virgin.

questions.q: According to the baraita in Bava Batra 14b, who wrote the Book of Job?
questions.why: It says Moses wrote his own book, the portion of Balaam and Job; the Talmud then records other views of when Job lived.

questions.q: According to the Letter of Aristeas, how many elders translated the Torah into Greek in Alexandria?
questions.why: Aristeas tells of six elders from each of the twelve tribes; the name Septuagint ("seventy") rounds the number.
